scope: Source-level audit of Passes 1-8 after Pass 9 exposed owner/helper fighting. No visual patching or repair performed by this audit.

overall_decision.reason: Pass 7 owner enforcement and Pass 8 helper enforcement are not fully complete at the live source/runtime level. Earlier passes also remain provisional until runtime receipts prove they are single-owner and current in the live app.

audit_results.name: Route/current path
evidence: pmp-current-map-v12.json marks the route guardian loader and current app as current.
pmp-current-inner-cleanbug-rgcontrols-v30-direct-boot-surface-20260708A.html publishes the current chain in source.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: Source path is current, but this audit did not read a live runtime localStorage route receipt after refresh. Full completion requires source + live receipt proof.

audit_results.name: Startup chain / launcher continuity
evidence: Current inner v30 contains a launch gate and App Orchestrator boot surface.
The frame loader injects many scripts and rescans on interval, so startup is not yet proven as a clean single-owner startup chain.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: Multiple loaders and interval injections remain active. Need a startup owner map proving which loader owns what and which ones are support-only.

audit_results.name: App Orchestrator as conductor
evidence: Current inner v30 publishes a live App Orchestrator API and writes pmp_app_orchestrator_v1_receipt.
The API itself says it does not perform ownership takeover.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: The App Orchestrator exists as a boot proof, but it is not yet enforcing owner/helper authority over all loaded legacy scripts.

audit_results.name: Mount Registry / legal slots
evidence: pmp-mount-registry-v1.js contains a static current/support file atlas.
Pass 9 showed panels can still appear in wrong order or wrong ownership location, so legal slots are not hard-enforced yet.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: Mount registry exists as an atlas, but legal slot enforcement is incomplete. It does not yet block helpers or legacy scripts from mounting/moving into wrong places.

audit_results.name: Diagnostics observes without controlling surfaces
evidence: pmp-diagnostics-owner-v1.js defines Diagnostics as an owner surface and reports no route/storage/Bank rebuild side effects.
pmp-safe-area-surface-fill-v1.js still removes exact leftover Control Diagnostics cards and repeats on interval.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: Diagnostics Owner may be mostly observer-only, but surrounding diagnostic/safe-area support still performs exact DOM cleanup. This must be classified so it is not confused with normal Diagnostics ownership.

audit_results.name: Safety / no destructive writes
evidence: Several sources state no route change, Bank rebuild, IndexedDB clear, or storage migration.
Active guard/repair/cleanup scripts still exist and some remove/hide/move exact DOM nodes.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: No destructive data write was found in this audit, but safety is not fully certified until active repair/guard scripts are mapped and constrained.

audit_results.name: Section owners: one owner per visible section
evidence: pmp-section-owner-registry-v1.js creates a boot snapshot, but only mount_registry_owner is marked present at boot.
The same snapshot lists missing_required_owners for other active owners.
pmp-pass7-certification-gate-v1.js explicitly distinguishes PASS7_CERTIFIED from PASS7_DEGRADED_READY and says bridge-seeded coverage may not be hard-certified.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: Pass 7 has owner rules/receipts, but it does not prove every live visible section has exactly one active owner at runtime. This is the core failure exposed by Pass 9.

audit_results.name: Helpers mapped and contained
evidence: pmp-helper-registry-v1.js boot receipt sets pass:false and lists helpers as missing/orphan in the boot snapshot.
pmp-pass8-helper-rules-v1.js is passive and explicitly says do_not_claim includes not enforcing blocking yet and not owner/helper source acceptance.
pmp-pass8-helper-rules-certification-v1.js depends on no unknown helpers and classified helpers, but current Pass 9 behavior proves enforcement is incomplete.
audit_results.blocker_to_full_completion: Pass 8 helper rules exist, but they are not a hard runtime blocker. Helpers/guards/legacy scripts can still move, hide, insert, or order DOM outside a verified owner handoff.

root_cause: Passes 1-8 were treated as complete because receipts and rule scaffolding existed. Source audit shows several passes are only passive/provisional and Passes 7-8 are not fully enforced. Pass 9 visual fighting is therefore not a Pass 9-only problem; it is an owner/helper enforcement gap from Passes 7-8, with earlier passes needing live proof revalidation.

required_next_step.name: Owner/Helper Conflict Map 001
required_next_step.purpose: List every active script, owner/helper/diagnostic/guard role, legal slot, actual DOM writes, interval/observer behavior, and conflicts before any more visual patching.
must_not_do: do not claim Pass 1-8 fully complete
do not keep patching visual order until owner/helper fighting is mapped
do not clear storage or IndexedDB
